*$NVDA | SEC launches a civil investigation into NVIDIA following Jensen Huang’s ouster, examining whether the company misled investors through inadequate disclosures — WSJ.*

• *SEC Investigation:* Regulators are examining potential violations of investor disclosure laws. The full scope remains unclear, but includes whether NVIDIA's statements misled shareholders. Shares have fallen more than 10% since Huang's departure.
• *Prior Denials:* NVIDIA previously denied that Huang had an unusual relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom US intelligence officials suspect of Chinese intelligence ties. Those suspicions remain unproven.
• *Singapore Scrutiny:* NVIDIA changed its geographic revenue reporting methodology last year, eliminating separate disclosure of Singapore-linked sales. Megaspeed has been under Commerce Department investigation since late 2024 over suspected chip diversions to China.
• *Federal Investigations:* The Justice Department is leading multiple investigations involving Alice Huang, while Congress is demanding answers about NVIDIA's chip sales and export controls.
• *Treasury Pressure:* Secretary Scott Bessent questioned whether NVIDIA knowingly facilitated restricted chip sales to boost earnings, demanding answers from its board and outside counsel within 10 days. No wrongdoing has been established.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA crushes Q3 FY2027 earnings estimates, with revenue surging 103% to $115.84B, Data Center sales jumping 110% and Q4 guidance topping Wall Street expectations.*

• *Revenue & Earnings:* Revenue of $115.84B beat $108.71B estimates by $7.13B (+6.6%), rising 103% YoY and 20% QoQ. Adjusted EPS of $2.68 beat $2.47 estimates by 8.5%, up 111% YoY. GAAP EPS reached $2.70, up 108%.
• *Data Center Growth:* Revenue surged 110% YoY and 21% QoQ to $107.6B, accounting for approximately 93% of total sales. Edge Computing revenue rose 42% YoY to $8.2B.
• *Profitability:* Adjusted gross margin reached 74.9%, nearly unchanged from 75.0% last quarter. Adjusted operating income jumped 116% to $77.9B, while GAAP net income climbed 105% to $65.3B.
• *Q4 Guidance:* NVIDIA forecasts $130B in revenue, ±3%, exceeding the $124.89B consensus by $5.11B (+4.1%). The outlook includes an extra fiscal week and assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China.
• *Margin Outlook:* Q4 GAAP and adjusted gross margins are projected at 71%–72%, down 290–390 basis points sequentially from Q3's adjusted margin. Adjusted operating expenses are expected at $10.7B, with GAAP expenses around $11B.
• *Vera Rubin Ramp:* NVIDIA says Vera Rubin NVL72 has begun shipping in its fastest product ramp ever. Systems are operating at CoreWeave ($CRWV), Google ($GOOGL), Microsoft ($MSFT), Oracle ($ORCL) and Nebius ($NBIS), with adoption expanding across Meta ($META), OpenAI, Anthropic and major hyperscalers.
• *Cash Generation:* Operating cash flow totaled $48.3B, including $43.8B in free cash flow, supporting continued AI infrastructure investment and shareholder returns.
• *Shareholder Returns:* NVIDIA returned $28.1B through buybacks and dividends during Q3. Its board previously authorized another $150B in repurchases, leaving $227.3B available at quarter-end.
• *Strategic Expansion:* NVIDIA is pursuing its previously announced Hugging Face acquisition to expand its AI platform ecosystem, while strengthening manufacturing partnerships with Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Amkor ($AMKR), Unimicron and other suppliers to support rising infrastructure demand.
• ⁠*Management Commentary:* Interim CEO Colette Kress said Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, with NVIDIA's roadmap on track and ambitions unchanged.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA discloses $518B in future commitments and up to $118B in contingent financial guarantees, revealing the scale of its investment in AI chip supplies, data centers and customer infrastructure.*

• *$518B in Commitments:* Includes $390B for supply and capacity, $74B in data center leases not yet commenced, $28B in cloud services, $20B in equity investments and $6B in capital expenditures. Supply commitments jumped from $279B last quarter, primarily for multiyear memory procurement.
• *Spending Timeline:* Approximately $82B is scheduled for the remainder of FY2027, $222B for FY2028 and $103B for FY2029. These are future commitments, some subject to contingencies, not expenses already incurred.
• *$118B in Guarantees:* Maximum gross contingent exposure includes $105B supporting SB Energy's Ohio project, $9.5B in power and systems financing and $3.5B in neocloud construction-related guarantees. Payments may be required if partners default. NVIDIA has made no payments under these guarantees.
• *OpenAI Infrastructure:* The $105B guarantee supports 4.25 GW across nine Ohio buildings hosting NVIDIA infrastructure under 20-year leases to OpenAI, subject to limited exceptions. Guarantees activate as individual buildings become ready, with the first expected in FY2029. Exposure then declines as OpenAI makes lease payments. NVIDIA has an option to support another 3.8 GW.
• *Neocloud Financing:* NVIDIA acknowledged that some neoclouds and AI labs are expanding faster than their financial capacity supports. It separately disclosed $32B in conditional neocloud agreements, dependent on financing, infrastructure deployment and acceptance. NVIDIA expects equipment sales revenue and may also receive a share of downstream customer revenue if additional criteria are met.
• *Cash Collection:* Accounts receivable reached $81B, with days sales outstanding rising from 60 to 64. NVIDIA attributed the increase to Rubin shipment timing and extended payment terms for certain investment-grade customers.
• *Inventory Build:* Inventory climbed from $31.6B to $39.7B sequentially to support Rubin production. Cash and marketable debt securities declined from $56.6B to $53.5B.
• *China Revenue:* NVIDIA shipped $2.4B in Hopper Data Center products to China during Q3, while its Q4 outlook assumes no China Data Center compute revenue.
• *Consumer Demand:* Higher memory and system prices continue weighing on consumer PC demand, while Blackwell workstations and physical AI applications support Edge Computing growth.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA's Q3 FY2027 revenue breakdown reveals AI cloud, industrial and enterprise sales nearly tripled, contributing more to annual Data Center growth than traditional hyperscalers.*

• *Hyperscale Revenue:* Sales to hyperscalers rose 71% YoY and 23% QoQ to $60.14B, representing 56% of Data Center revenue.
• *AI Cloud & Enterprise Surge:* Revenue from AI clouds, industrial and enterprise customers jumped 195% YoY and 18% QoQ to $47.47B. This segment now represents 44% of Data Center sales, up from 31% a year earlier.
• *Growth Drivers:* AI cloud, industrial and enterprise customers contributed $31.4B of Data Center's $56.4B annual revenue increase (56%), exceeding the $25B increase from hyperscalers.
• *Quarterly Momentum:* Total revenue climbed $19.62B QoQ, with Data Center accounting for $18.59B of that increase (95%). Hyperscalers contributed $11.43B in sequential growth, versus $7.16B from AI cloud, industrial and enterprise customers.
• *Edge Computing:* Revenue rose 42% YoY and 14% QoQ to $8.23B, accounting for the remaining 7% of total revenue.
• *Reporting Adjustment:* NVIDIA revised its market classifications in Q1 FY2027 and moved one customer from AI cloud/enterprise to hyperscale in Q2 following a change in its business model, recasting historical figures for comparability.
• *Key Takeaway:* Hyperscalers still generate the most revenue, but AI cloud, industrial and enterprise customers are driving faster annual growth, broadening NVIDIA's revenue base beyond traditional hyperscalers.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA's Q3 FY2027 presentation reveals accelerating enterprise AI demand, nearly $20B in sequential Vera Rubin revenue growth and plans to deploy $227B in remaining share buybacks through FY2028.*

• *AI Customer Breakdown:* Hyperscaler revenue rose 71% YoY to $60.1B, while AI cloud, industrial and enterprise revenue surged 195% to $47.5B. The latter contributed roughly 56% of Data Center's annual revenue increase, signaling demand growth beyond traditional hyperscalers.
• *Vera Rubin Momentum:* NVIDIA says Vera Rubin added nearly $20B in revenue QoQ, making it the fastest product ramp in company history. Rubin NVL72 also delivered up to twice Blackwell Ultra's per-GPU performance in its MLPerf Training debut.
• *Capacity Utilization:* NVIDIA says its deployed compute infrastructure remains fully utilized, supporting its argument that demand remains strong even as newer GPU generations enter production.
• *Improving Product Mix:* Q3 adjusted gross margin increased 1.4 percentage points YoY to 74.9%, driven by a more favorable Blackwell Ultra product mix. GAAP gross margin also improved 1.4 points to 74.8%.
• *Operating Leverage:* Adjusted operating expenses rose 52% YoY to $8.8B, significantly slower than revenue growth of 103%. Adjusted operating income consequently jumped 116% to $77.9B.
• *Infrastructure Investment:* Capital expenditures for property, equipment and intangibles increased to $4.42B from $1.64B a year earlier, reflecting expanded investment in NVIDIA's operations and capacity.
• *Buyback Timeline:* Free cash flow nearly doubled to $43.8B from $22.1B. NVIDIA plans to utilize its approximately $227B remaining share repurchase authorization through FY2028.
• *Accounting Detail:* A $1.77B gain on equity securities helped lift GAAP EPS to $2.70, above adjusted EPS of $2.68. NVIDIA also clarified that its adjusted earnings now include stock-based compensation, with historical figures updated for comparability.
• *Risk Disclosures:* NVIDIA explicitly identifies CEO succession, executive retention, regulatory investigations and litigation among the uncertainties that could affect future results.

*$NVDA | Former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang can nominate two independent directors to the company's board, potentially retaining influence over its leadership despite his resignation — Reuters.*

• *Ownership Rights:* Huang and entities tied to him hold approximately 3.5% of NVIDIA, exceeding the 3% ownership threshold maintained for at least three years required to nominate directors through the company's proxy process.
• *Board Influence:* Huang can nominate two independent candidates for inclusion on NVIDIA's annual shareholder ballot, typically held in June. Directors oversee corporate strategy and CEO appointments.
• *Approval Required:* Nominations do not guarantee board seats. Shareholders must elect the candidates, and NVIDIA can exclude nominees who violate its bylaws or charter.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA raises its FY2028 revenue growth outlook to approximately 75% from 70%, citing accelerating AI demand, expanding cloud backlogs and stronger infrastructure supply.*

• *Revenue Outlook:* The revised forecast implies roughly $730B in FY2028 annual revenue, or $183B quarterly, assuming FY2027 finishes at its Q4 guidance midpoint. This is an implied calculation, not a separate dollar-denominated company forecast.
• *Cloud Backlog:* NVIDIA says industrywide cloud backlog reached $2.5T, up from $2T three months ago, signaling expanding multiyear infrastructure demand.
• *Frontier AI Labs:* NVIDIA expects major frontier labs to contribute approximately 15% of its Data Center revenue this year. Management cited Anthropic's annualized revenue reaching $81B in October as evidence of growing AI adoption.
• *Agentic AI Growth:* Weekly token volume on OpenRouter reportedly increased 35-fold YoY and 3.5-fold over three months. Agentic workloads now account for approximately 80% of tokens in the cited ecosystem.
• *CPU Demand:* NVIDIA expects CPU revenue to more than double in FY2028 as agentic AI drives demand for CPUs that management says is far outstripping available supply.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA says GPU rental prices are rising sharply even as AI token prices have fallen nearly 60% since May, as cheaper AI usage drives greater demand for computing capacity.*

• *Token Economics:* AI token prices have declined nearly 60% since May, according to NVIDIA, accelerating consumption as AI workloads become cheaper to run.
• *Hopper Pricing:* Hopper GPUs have been re-contracted at up to twice their original rental prices under multiyear agreements, suggesting sustained demand for older-generation chips.
• *Blackwell Pricing:* B300 GPU rental rates have increased more than 60% since introduction, despite expanding availability of newer architectures.
• *Capacity Utilization:* NVIDIA says its compute remains fully utilized across every hyperscaler and neocloud it serves, including infrastructure operated by CoreWeave ($CRWV), Nebius ($NBIS) and other cloud partners.
• *Market Implication:* Lower costs per AI token are encouraging greater usage, while demand for the underlying GPU capacity continues to exceed available supply.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA signals a more disciplined and selective approach to neocloud financial support while expanding its agentic AI infrastructure and security ecosystem.*

• *Neocloud Strategy:* NVIDIA says it will be selective in supporting neocloud expansion. Its agreements depend on customers securing financing and deploying operational infrastructure, with certain commitments potentially reduced or eliminated if conditions are not met.
• *Agent Security:* NVIDIA introduced its OpenAgent Safety Platform alongside more than 100 partners. OpenShell restricts AI agents' access to files and tools, while NVIDIA Sentry on BlueField-4 monitors behavior and can stop agents that exceed permitted boundaries within milliseconds.
• *Ecosystem Partners:* Companies working with NVIDIA include Anthropic, AWS ($AMZN), CoreWeave ($CRWV), CrowdStrike ($CRWD), Google ($GOOGL), IREN ($IREN), Microsoft ($MSFT), Nebius ($NBIS), OpenAI and SpaceX.
• *Meta Adoption:* Meta's ($META) Muse agent reportedly exceeded 10M setups across the US and Canada in its first six weeks. Meta intends to expand Vera Rubin deployments to support growing AI-agent workloads.
• *Strategic Direction:* NVIDIA is expanding beyond chips into security, agent infrastructure and supporting software while maintaining conditions on financial commitments to AI cloud customers.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA says it is no longer shipping licensed Hopper Data Center products to China, confirming an active halt rather than merely excluding future sales from guidance.*

• *Q3 Shipments:* NVIDIA generated $2.4B from licensed Hopper Data Center product shipments to China during the quarter.
• *Current Status:* Interim CEO Colette Kress confirmed these shipments have stopped, with none included in Q4 guidance.
• *Scope:* The statement specifically concerns licensed Hopper Data Center products, not every NVIDIA product sold in China. Management did not provide a resumption timeline.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA says Vera Rubin delivers 10 times more AI tokens per watt than GB300 in the MLPerf Endpoints benchmark, while reaffirming plans for Rubin Ultra in 2027 and Feynman in 2028.*

• *Efficiency Breakthrough:* NVIDIA cited 10x higher tokens per watt versus GB300 on the MLPerf Endpoints benchmark, highlighting improvements in inference efficiency rather than a universal 10x performance gain.
• *Deployment Progress:* Rubin production shipments began in August. Three months later, systems are reaching major hyperscaler and leading neocloud data centers.
• *Next Architectures:* NVIDIA remains on track to introduce Vera Rubin Ultra in 2027, followed by Feynman in 2028.
• *Further Optimization:* Management expects software improvements to increase Rubin performance throughout its lifecycle.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA expands supply-chain agreements with Kinsus, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and SPIL to address shortages in chip substrates and advanced packaging as AI infrastructure demand outpaces supply.*

• *New Agreements:* Management highlighted substrate arrangements with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics, alongside advanced packaging cooperation with SPIL.
• *Kinsus Timeline:* Production is expected to begin in H2 2027, with expanded capacity targeted for Q3 2028, according to the call-related reports.
• *Existing Partners:* These arrangements build on previously announced agreements involving Amkor ($AMKR), IBIDEN, KYEC and Unimicron.
• *Capacity Expansion:* Amkor targets more than 300% growth in interposer wafer capacity by year-end 2028, while SPIL aims to expand optical-engine capacity 15-fold by mid-2027.
• *Strategic Objective:* NVIDIA is securing substrates, packaging and testing capacity to increase AI hardware production and reduce supply-chain bottlenecks.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA expects enterprise revenue to more than double in FY2028 as financial services, quantitative trading and physical AI adoption accelerate.*

• *Financial Services:* On-premises revenue from financial services nearly reached $5B over the trailing 12 months, more than doubling YoY. NVIDIA cited growing demand for infrastructure supporting quantitative trading.
• *Enterprise Outlook:* Management expects enterprise revenue to more than double in FY2028 as adoption broadens across industries.
• *Physical AI:* Revenue nearly tripled YoY in Q3 and is on track to exceed $25B for the full fiscal year.
• *Robotics:* NVIDIA expanded its Isaac robotics platform with a humanoid reference design using Isaac GR00T and Jetson Thor.
• *Autonomous Vehicles:* NVIDIA highlighted work involving Mercedes-Benz, Bolt with Lucid, autonomous trucking and Volvo Cars through its Hyperion and Alpamayo platforms.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA provides new details on its neocloud financing model, combining infrastructure sales with potential rental-revenue participation while tightening investment discipline.*

• *Revenue Sharing:* NVIDIA says its neocloud agreements allow it to earn revenue from upfront infrastructure sales and participate in rental revenue above a minimum commitment, subject to contractual conditions.
• *Ohio Development:* SB Energy expects capacity at its Ohio campus supporting OpenAI to come online in phases beginning in calendar 2028. NVIDIA's related guarantees activate separately as buildings become ready for service.
• *Capital Discipline:* Management says it is rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees as additional third-party financing becomes available.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA expects Q4 FY2027 to mark the bottom for gross margins, forecasting a recovery to 72%–73% in FY2028 despite new US chip export restrictions.*

• *Margin Recovery:* Q4 GAAP and adjusted gross margins are projected at 71%–72%, with management expecting both to improve into the 72%–73% range in FY2028.
• *Demand Outlook:* Kress said AI infrastructure demand continues to exceed supply, supporting NVIDIA's expectation of sustained growth despite the latest Commerce Department export restrictions.
• *FY2028 Forecast:* NVIDIA raised its annual revenue growth outlook to approximately 75% from 70%, applied to a higher FY2027 revenue base.
• *Implied Revenue:* Using reported quarterly results and the $130B Q4 guidance midpoint, FY2027 revenue would approach $424B. Applying 75% growth implies roughly $742B in FY2028 sales. This is a calculated estimate, not NVIDIA's explicit dollar guidance.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA interim CEO Colette Kress says business remains on track despite Jensen Huang's departure, citing continued employee commitment and strong support from customers and suppliers.*

• *Leadership Transition:* Chairman Harvey Jones said NVIDIA will evaluate internal and external CEO candidates. Ian Buck, VP of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing, joined Kress on the earnings call.
• *Employee Retention:* Kress expressed confidence that NVIDIA's engineers and executives remain committed, emphasizing its world-class technical talent and multiyear product roadmap.
• *Supplier Support:* TSMC ($TSM) leadership visited NVIDIA's offices this week and remains fully engaged. Kress said memory and advanced packaging supply are secured.
• *Business Continuity:* Management said customers and suppliers remain supportive, with NVIDIA maintaining its development roadmap and execution priorities throughout the transition.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA says it absorbed higher supply costs to honor existing customer purchase orders, with new pricing expected to take effect as it moves into FY2028.*

• *Existing Contracts:* Interim CEO Colette Kress said NVIDIA absorbed some rising supply costs rather than changing pricing on purchase orders already received from customers.
• *Pricing Transition:* Management is moving toward new pricing in the coming fiscal year, allowing it to adjust pricing arrangements after honoring earlier commitments.
• *Competitive Pressure:* The explanation came in response to an analyst questioning NVIDIA's long-term pricing power and margins as frontier AI developers increasingly adopt custom ASICs and prioritize compute efficiency.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA identifies land, power and data center construction as priority areas for potential financial support, while clarifying that its conditional neocloud guarantee terms are not new.*

• *Financing Priorities:* Colette Kress identified securing land, electricity and data center building infrastructure as critical to AI expansion and among NVIDIA's top areas to evaluate for financial assistance.
• *Investment-Grade Customers:* NVIDIA said creditworthy enterprise customers could help finance construction through advance payments, reducing the capital required from developers and neocloud operators.
• *Selective Support:* NVIDIA continues working with neoclouds but is reassessing which companies and projects warrant financing assistance. Management emphasized reviewing counterparties and project fundamentals rather than committing capital broadly.
• *Guarantee Conditions:* NVIDIA clarified that its guarantees become effective only after required financing, construction and deployment milestones are met. If projects cannot proceed or face qualifying delays, the associated guarantees may not take effect or may cease to apply.
• *No Policy Change:* Asked whether the newly emphasized conditions reflected a change in business practices, Kress said they were existing terms being clarified in response to investor questions.
• ⁠*Key Distinction:* NVIDIA is not abandoning neocloud financing, but neither is it promising support to every developer. Financial commitments remain tied to project readiness and contractual conditions.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA identifies supplier prepayments as a major capital priority, aiming to accelerate manufacturing capacity as demand for AI hardware continues to strain production.*

• *Supplier Funding:* Interim CEO Colette Kress said NVIDIA may provide advance payments and other capital assistance to manufacturers to help expand production capacity faster.
• *Capital Priorities:* Management emphasized supplier funding as a particularly valuable use of capital, reflecting the importance of bringing additional hardware supply online.
• *Financing Allocation:* Kress said customer financing and guarantees are expected to represent a relatively small portion of NVIDIA's broader capital deployment.

*$NVDA | NVIDIA says major AI customers were requesting additional computing capacity as recently as last week, while management acknowledges growing community concerns surrounding US data center expansion.*

• *Recent Customer Requests:* Kress said major customers continued asking how NVIDIA could deliver more hardware to meet demand from new AI models and autonomous-agent applications.
• *Existing Facilities:* Management pointed to data centers already operating or ready for deployment as potential sources of capacity to support customer demand.
• *Community Concerns:* NVIDIA acknowledged questions about how new data centers affect surrounding communities, including employment opportunities and local acceptance.
• *Government Coordination:* Kress said NVIDIA will continue engaging government officials and encouraging cooperation among developers and communities as AI infrastructure expands.

*Microsoft ($MSFT) executive says NVIDIA's leadership turmoil could accelerate customers' shift toward competing AI chips, reinforcing demand for alternatives to its dominant GPU ecosystem — Bloomberg.*

• *Customer Sentiment:* Microsoft commercial CEO Judson Althoff said customers were already seeking alternatives before Jensen Huang's departure, with the scandal reinforcing their desire to diversify.
• *Chip Competition:* Microsoft, Amazon ($AMZN) and Google ($GOOGL) are developing proprietary AI chips to reduce NVIDIA dependence. AMD ($AMD) and Broadcom ($AVGO) could also benefit as customers reassess suppliers.
• *Microsoft Strategy:* Althoff said AI model and chip diversity will become increasingly important. Microsoft previously outlined plans to run most of its AI software on internally developed hardware.
• *Partnership Outlook:* Althoff said customers are largely waiting for NVIDIA's governance issues to settle, while emphasizing that Microsoft intends to maintain its partnership with the company.
• *Ignite Announcements:* Microsoft also introduced proprietary AI models it claims are more cost-effective than offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic, positioning its platform to support competing AI technologies.

*NVIDIA ($NVDA) INTERIM CEO COLETTE KRESS: DEMAND RISING, CUSTOMERS STAYING*

Speaking with CNBC’s Jim Cramer on Nov. 17, Kress addressed customer demand and Nvidia’s outlook following Jensen Huang’s departure.

• *Customers:* “This concept that anything is changing in terms of any of our types of customers: that is just not true.” She added that “customers continue to be with us.”
• *Demand:* “The most important thing we have seen is growth in the demand that’s out there.”
• *Supply:* “What we need in terms of chips, what we need in terms of advanced packaging or memory, all of that is also coming together.”
• *Growth Outlook:* “We felt very confident, therefore, that we could establish that we will grow 75% over year over year in terms of fiscal year 28.” Nvidia raised its FY2028 growth forecast from 70% to 75%.
• *Business Continuity:* Kress also told investors it was “business as usual at Nvidia,” adding: “Remember, we have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap.”

*NVIDIA ($NVDA) INTERIM CEO COLETTE KRESS: BOARD WILL NOT REINSTATE JENSEN HUANG*

In a CNBC interview, Jim Cramer asked whether Huang could return in another role, such as chief technologist or ambassador, rather than CEO.

*Kress:* “Jensen resigned from his position with Nvidia and the board accepted his resignation. The board has determined that they will not reinstate Jensen, and that is our statement and what the board has decided to do.”

Kress added: “We want to think about right now growing our business. We want to grow in terms of everything that we need to do with our employees, our customers, our shareholders, and that is where we are gonna focus moving forward.”

*Sequoia, Iconiq, Lightspeed, Accel and Altimeter plan to buy billions of dollars in Anthropic’s IPO, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter.*

• *Existing Investments:* Iconiq has invested over $6B, Lightspeed over $3.5B and Sequoia $3B for roughly a 1% stake. Accel’s investment is its largest ever, though the amount is undisclosed.
